posts.title: What makes Brazilian house cleaning different?
posts.text:
People in Startex, SC ask us this a lot: what is Brazilian house cleaning, and how is it different from a regular maid service? The short answer is that it is detail first and done by hand.

Instead of spraying and wiping the obvious surfaces, our team wipes each surface by hand, works the corners and edges with a cloth, and moves small items to clean under them. Door frames, light switches and handles get attention, bathrooms are scrubbed down to the grout and the toilet base, and the kitchen is degreased around the stovetop, hood and cabinet fronts. Floors are washed by hand along the walls, where dust collects first. Before we leave, we walk the house against a room checklist.

This method suits homes with hardwood, tile and grout, and families who have been let down by a rushed clean. Many houses around the Startex mill village and the Duncan and Lyman area have details worth the extra care.

posts.title: One house cleaning tip for Greer homes this fall
posts.text:
Looking for reliable house cleaning in Greer, SC? Here is one tip our team shares with every new client: clean from top to bottom, and from dry to wet.

Start with ceiling fans, shelves and the tops of door frames, then wipe counters, and vacuum and mop the floors last. Dust always falls, so working downward means you never clean the same surface twice. Save the wet work (bathrooms, kitchen sink, mopping) for the end, so dust doesn't stick to damp surfaces.

That is the same order Perfect Services follows in homes across Greer, from older houses near Trade Street to newer neighborhoods off SC-14 and SC-101. Our Brazilian, detail-first method adds the parts a rushed clean skips: baseboards, cabinet handles, light switches and the edges along every floor.
